name: WebGL
notes: VERIFIED WORKING on this machine. Probe: Playwright's headless Chromium 151.0.7922.34 (already present in ~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright, so nothing was downloaded), page at about:blank, canvas.getContext('webgl2') returned a context reporting VERSION='WebGL 2.0 (OpenGL ES 3.0 Chromium)', RENDERER='WebKit WebGL', MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE=8192. That is a software-rasterised context, which is enough to prove the API path works and not enough to say anything about GPU performance. `version` stays null because a platform API has no installable artifact to version — the measured VERSION string is above. For the same reason P2 ("version is non-null") is unreachable here, and because the ladder runs through P2, P3 is unreachable too: readiness is therefore P1, matching the other browser platform APIs (SVG 78, HTML Canvas 79, WebGPU 143, WebSocket API 409, WebRTC 410). This record was written as P3 and was lowered at merge time rather than given an invented version. verification_status stays smoke-tested because the probe above genuinely ran and passed; that evidence is not withdrawn, it just does not earn a level whose bar is a measured version. license is null and flagged: nothing is distributed to license, and the specification text is under Khronos's own terms rather than a software licence.

name: WebGPU
notes: NOT verified — and the negative result is about the probe, not the machine. Two attempts in Playwright's headless Chromium 151.0.7922.34: default flags, then --enable-unsafe-webgpu --enable-features=Vulkan,WebGPU --use-angle=metal. Both returned 'gpu' in navigator === false, so requestAdapter() was never reachable. WebGL 2.0 came up in the same context (id 142), which isolates the failure to WebGPU rather than to graphics in general: headless Chromium gates WebGPU behind a GPU process this launch does not start. Do not read this as 'WebGPU is unavailable on this machine' — a headed browser on macOS 26.4.1 is the test that would settle it, and it was not run. license is null and flagged for the same reason as id 142: a platform API distributes nothing to license.

Reproducible: in a Lake project on a matching toolchain, `require mathlib from git "https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4"` then `lake exe cache get` to pull prebuilt oleans instead of compiling. Mathlib tracks Lean releases tightly, so the revision must match Lean 4.33.0 (id 201). Open question worth closing before anyone depends on this: whether the hosted AXLE environment 'lean-4.33.0' ships Mathlib is NOT verified — it was not probed from this machine, and the repository's proofs use core Nat lemmas that do not need it.
